recent_posts.title: eBay launches sneaker authentication service to combat counterfeit sales
recent_posts.summary: eBay is launching a new sneaker authentication service to verify that shoes sold on the platform match what their listings claim. The service will start the week of October 25th and cover the most popular sneaker styles and brands. By early 2021 it will expand to cover all sneakers sold for over $100 on eBay in the US.

recent_posts.title: Samsung’s Galaxy Note 10 is down to $550 at eBay
recent_posts.summary: Samsung’s Galaxy Note 10 is available for $550 on eBay. Normally the phone costs $950 and previously we have seen the price go down to as low as $600. This is for an unlocked version of the phone compatible with all of the major LTE networks in the US.

recent_posts.title: In a rare move, a Netflix original will stream on free streaming service Pluto TV
recent_posts.summary: Narcos will be available to stream for free on ViacomCBS’s Pluto TV beginning on October 20th. The deal marks the first time that the show will be widely available to US streaming viewers without a Netflix subscription and for free. The first season will stream weeknights at 10PM ET. Catch-up episodes will be made available the following day beginning at 8pm ET.

recent_posts.title: Panasonic has made it way easier to use Lumix cameras as webcams
recent_posts.summary: Panasonic has released an official Lumix webcam app, as first spotted by PetaPixel. The software, still in beta since its quiet release late last month, lets you plug your camera into your Mac or Windows machine and have it recognized as a video source. Panasonic’s official software replaces the workaround hack the company introduced back in June.

recent_posts.title: Exclusive: Wisconsin denies Foxconn tax subsidies after contract negotiations fail
recent_posts.summary: Wisconsin rejected Foxconn’s application for tax subsidies on the grounds that the company had not carried out the Gen 10.5 LCD factory project described in its original contract. Foxconn needed to employ at least 520 people at the end of 2019 to receive subsidies and claimed to have hired 550, but WEDC estimated that only 281 would qualify.

recent_posts.title: Head of Russian space program calls for more international cooperation in NASA’s Moon plans
recent_posts.summary: Dmitry Rogozin, the director-general of Roscosmos, said today that NASA’s plans to send people back to the Moon are “too US-centric” He has been critical of the program in the past and now says that Russia would only be open to participating if the Moon plans were more focused on international cooperation. “The most important thing here would be to base this program on the principles of international cooperation”

recent_posts.title: Rez Infinite is still a VR classic on the Oculus Quest
recent_posts.summary: The Oculus Quest version of Rez Infinite is coming just in time for the release of the new Quest 2 headset. The Quest version will be released on Tuesday, October 13th — the same day as the Quest 2. Rez Infinite has been a VR staple ever since it launched alongside the PlayStation VR in 2016.

recent_posts.title: Google’s Nest announces new smart thermostat with simpler design, lower price
recent_posts.summary: Google’s Nest smart home division has a new smart thermostat available to order starting today. The new Nest Thermostat is a simpler model than the Nest Learning Thermostats and comes with a lower price, just $129.99. Gone is the traditional rotating dial and in its place is a touch sensitive strip that is used to navigate the interface and make adjustments.

recent_posts.title: What to expect from Apple’s iPhone 12 event
recent_posts.summary: Apple’s next fall event kicks off tomorrow at 1PM ET. The company is widely expected to reveal its new iPhone 12 lineup of smartphones. Rumors have given us a pretty good picture of what we can expect to see with these new phones. All of the iPhones are expected to support speedier 5G cellular networks. Apple could also announce the official release date for iOS 14.2.

recent_posts.title: Twitter flags, limits sharing on Trump tweet about being “immune” to coronavirus
recent_posts.summary: Twitter disabled some sharing options on a tweet from President Trump on Sunday. In the tweet, the president said he had “A total and complete sign off from White House Doctors yesterday. That means I can’t get it (immune) and can”t give it.” Even with the label, the tweet is still available for those who click through the warning.

top_posts.title: Among Us is so popular that its developers just canceled the sequel
top_posts.summary: Among Us is the third most-played game on Steam. The game has more than 10 million owners on Steam alone. Even though the sequel has been canned, you’ll still be able to eventually play the game its developers were hoping to build. The developer also promised fixes for server issues, colorblind support, a friends system, and a whole new stage.

top_posts.title: G Suite is now Google Workspace in a bid to merge Gmail, Chat, and Docs
top_posts.summary: Google is rebranding G Suite with a new name: Google Workspace. Along with the new branding are new features for Gmail, Docs, Meet, Sheets, and Calendar. Google is also changing up its pricing tiers just a bit, adding a new “Business Plus” level with more device management features.

top_posts.title: Google will give you the new Chromecast for free if you pay for one month of YouTube TV
top_posts.summary: All you have to do is sign up for YouTube TV and pay for one month of the service. You then have to make a payment toward your YouTube TV subscription between October 15th and December 31st in order to receive the offer for the free Chromecast. The deal is only available in the US.

top_posts.title: Wikipedia is getting its first desktop redesign in 10 years
top_posts.summary: Wikipedia is getting a makeover for the first time in a decade to make the site more approachable for new users. A collapsible sidebar will be the first change to roll out. The site will also add an easy one-click button to switch the language for a page you’re reading.

top_posts.title: Studio Ghibli releases 400 free-to-use images from eight of its classic films, with more to come
top_posts.summary: The images come from From Up On Poppy Hill, Ponyo, Spirited Away, The Tale of The Princess Kaguya, The Secret World of Arrietty, Tales From Earthsea, When Marnie Was There, and The Wind Rises. Studio Ghibli says it will release images from all of its films over time.
